bear_case.title: The revenue gap
bear_case.description: Hyperscalers are now tracking toward $750–900B of 2026 capex against roughly $51B of direct AI revenue generated — a gap that widened further after Amazon, Alphabet and Meta all raised guidance again in late July. The BIS estimates the top-5 hyperscalers will spend over $1T combined across 2025–2026 and names an AI-capex bust as one of its top three risks to global financial stability.

bear_case.title: A market that's turned selective, not just skeptical
bear_case.description: Alphabet's Jul 22 capex hike helped erase $787B from the Magnificent Seven in a single session on Jul 23 — the group's worst day in over a year. Yet a week later Microsoft (+8%) and Amazon (+10%) were rewarded for the same kind of guidance hike, while Meta fell ~9–10% despite beating on revenue. The market isn't punishing capex outright anymore — it's punishing capex without a visible growth payoff (Azure, AWS) more than capex with one.

bear_case.title: Off-balance-sheet obligations
bear_case.description: Moody's flags ~$662B of signed-but-not-commenced data-center lease commitments sitting off hyperscaler balance sheets. Oracle's own disclosure is a live example: a $638B AI backlog, boosted by a $300B OpenAI deal, of which only ~12% converts to revenue within 12 months — obligations booked well ahead of cash.

bear_case.title: Circular financing
bear_case.description: Interlocking vendor-equity stakes and take-or-pay compute deals among NVIDIA, Microsoft, OpenAI, Anthropic, Oracle and CoreWeave — echoing the Lucent/Nortel vendor-financing dynamics of 1999–2001 — make end-demand look larger and more independent than it is. Oracle's $300B OpenAI compute deal, funded in part by an estimated $40B external capital raise, is the latest data point. Analysts now peg the web of circular deals at over $800B, and the BIS flags a "circular financing collapse" as a top-three global financial-stability risk.

bear_case.title: Depreciation clock
bear_case.description: Hyperscalers depreciate AI hardware over 5–6 years, but bears (Michael Burry among them) argue the chips' real economic life is closer to 1–3 years — an estimated ~$176B understatement of depreciation across 2026–2028 that flatters reported earnings. The first defaults could surface in 2027–2028 as initial lease terms come up for renewal.

bear_case.title: Concentration everywhere
bear_case.description: AI is simultaneously the market's largest index weight, VC's largest allocation (~80% of a record $510B global H1 2026 venture total), and this hub's connective thread — a drawdown would hit robotics, nuclear, storage, and quantum sentiment at once. Counterpoint: infrastructure vendors keep posting record quarters (TSMC's guide raise, AWS's fastest growth in 18 quarters) — some strategists call the bear thesis premature given actual demand signals.

catalysts.title: Big Tech earnings week delivers a split verdict
catalysts.description: Microsoft (+8%) and Amazon (+10%, AWS's fastest growth in 18 quarters, capex raised to $220B) were rewarded; Meta fell ~9–10% despite a $60.8B revenue beat after raising its own capex guide to $125–145B. The market is now discriminating between capex tied to visible growth and capex that isn't.

catalysts.title: Magnificent Seven's worst day in over a year
catalysts.description: Alphabet's capex hike to $195–205B, paired with Tesla's own capex warning, erased $787B in Magnificent Seven market value in a single session — a 4.8% drop, the steepest since April 2025.

catalysts.title: Oracle's AI backlog hits $638B
catalysts.description: Driven largely by a new $300B OpenAI compute deal; only ~12% is expected to convert to revenue within 12 months, and Oracle is estimated to need a ~$40B external capital raise to fund ~$95B of this fiscal year's capex.

catalysts.title: AMD and SpaceX both report

positions.name: NVIDIA
positions.note: Data Center revenue $75.2B in Q1 FY27 (+92% YoY). Every hyperscaler capex plan still starts here; Aug 26 earnings is the first real test since July's semiconductor retreat.

positions.name: TSMC
positions.note: Makes the chips for everyone on this page. Q2 revenue $40.2B (+34%), FY guidance raised above 40% growth. Taiwan is the single largest tail risk in your entire hub.

positions.name: Alphabet
positions.note: The only genuinely full-stack position — TPUs, Gemini, DeepMind, Waymo — and the least dependent on buying someone else's compute.

positions.name: Microsoft
positions.note: ~40% Azure growth against a defensible capex ask. The open question is whether the market still rewards that once FY27's $255–260B is actually on the table.

positions.name: Amazon
positions.note: AWS grew 37%, its fastest in 18 quarters, and quarterly revenue topped $200B for the first time. Cheapest way to own AI demand inside a business that already prints cash.

positions.name: Broadcom
positions.note: Custom ASICs for Apple, Meta, Alphabet, ByteDance and OpenAI plus AI networking. The hedge against any single GPU vendor losing share.

positions.name: AMD
positions.note: A credible number two, +114% in 2026 and outpacing NVDA. That outperformance is the risk, not the thesis — much is already in the price.

positions.name: Palantir
positions.note: Real government and commercial revenue attached to a multiple that assumes near-flawless execution for years. Conviction in the business, not in the entry point.

positions.name: Oracle
positions.note: Genuine AI backlog, funded substantially with debt. If Gurley's financing argument is right anywhere, it is right here first.

positions.name: Meta
positions.note: Enormous capex with the least direct route to AI revenue of any hyperscaler — the model has to sell more ads to pay for itself.

positions.name: UiPath
positions.note: Being disrupted by the agent wave it markets itself as part of.
